newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -Gilts to shoot higher while 115-02 holds.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Gilts to shoot higher while 115-02 holds.

text.p: September gilt futures on LIFFE are strongly underpinned by support in the 115-02/10 zone and will aim higher while this holds, analysts said on Friday.
David Sneddon, technical analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston in London, said 115-02/10 marked a key gap when the market spiked higher this week and a plethora of supports.

"This is quite a big area that we've got in here," said Sneddon. "While it's above there, then this is just a pull back and we're looking for a move back to (eventually) 116-30, with 115-23/25 being the interim resistance," he said.
At 0700 GMT, September gilts opened 2/32 down at 115-09.
While 115-23 and 115-25 are the twin peaks reached on Wednesday and Thursday, resistance at 116-30 is much stronger as it is defined by an 11-year downtrend, Sneddon said.
A break of 115-23 would confirm the current slide is a shallow pullback, he said.

"Should we see 115-02 go, you're going to get a pull back to the 114-16/20 region, but then I would look for a strong bias to come again," said Sneddon, adding that the market did not seem to want a deeper correction just yet.
"We've got to stick our toes in the water now, it's probably not worth not being long," said Sneddon.
Sneddon said European bond markets in general were nervous after recent rallies, but gilts fared better than most and were likely to outperform Bunds.
September broke out of a heavy congestion area this week, setting a new contract high of 115-25, but came down on Thursday to finish at 115-11.
Richard Adcock, manager, technical research at HSBC Futures said in a note it was possible the consolidation would continue.
"But with good support in place down to the figure and the longer term picture bullish we feel this setback offers buying opportunities with stops placed under 114-23," said Adcock.
He saw initial trendline support at 115-06, followed more mildly by 114-23 and 114-16.
At the short end, December short sterling was quoted at 92.62, unchanged on the day.

Adcock said while support at 92.56 held, a continuation of the sideways action could be foreseen over the next few days with moves to 92.65 offering further selling opportunities with stops placed over 92.70.
